title: Harness prompt assembly buries the operator task under directive preamble + memory-as-user-turn — smaller models conclude "no task provided"
wanted_capability: The dispatched prompt should be unmistakably demarcated as THE task, not appended unmarked after stacked directives. Observed (session 7476e678, vibebh/mistral-medium-3.5, openai-chat): first user turn = 2,845 chars of [scope]+[recall before acting]+[task shape]+[completion contract]+[milestone reporting] with the operator's one-line instruction as the bare last line; second user turn = 15,434 chars of rendered provider memory; the model answered "the user hasn't actually provided a task yet" and wandered. The same model follows the same instruction fine in its native CLI (clean prompt), so this is harness prompt assembly, not model capability. Candidate fixes (design decision): (a) explicit [task] demarcation or task-first ordering with directives after; (b) move standing directives to the system message on transports that support it (openai-chat allows a leading system message; the Mistral constraint only bans system-after-tool); (c) deliver rendered memory via the system/project-doc lane instead of a synthetic user turn. Compounding friction in the same trace: bbox_thread_list was deferred, so the task's one required tool cost an unknown-tool error + tool_search round-trip before work could start.
fallback_used: none — misattributed to model quality until the operator pushed back; events.jsonl forensics corrected it

notes:
CORRECTION from reading actual Codex source (~/repos/codex, codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs ~2860, context/user_instructions.rs, context/contextual_user_message.rs): the prior provenance note overstated. Codex does NOT stuff policy into user turns — it has a typed PromptSlot system (DeveloperPolicy / DeveloperCapabilities / SeparateDeveloper / ContextualUser): its own standing policy+capability prose rides DEVELOPER-role messages (build_developer_update_item) plus base_instructions on the request. Only user-authored/situational content rides the contextual USER message — UserInstructions (AGENTS.md, semantically user-authored) and EnvironmentContext — each wrapped in typed markers with a fragment registry, assembled into ONE contextual message SEPARATE from the operator's prompt item. Our harness imported only "instructions can be a user message" with none of the discipline.

FIX DESIGNED (2026-06-11, reviewed clean): design/bro-harness/dispatch-prompt-slots.md. Daemon passes typed ingredients only (--dispatch-context v1 JSON: persona / directives with cadence+needs_scope / scope fields / pins); harness owns composition via per-transport strategy. Two v1 strategies: codex-shaped (anthropic, responses — persona+standing directives in stable system, per_turn directives in volatile tail, scope/pins as marker-demarcated contextual-user fragments) and vibe-shaped (openai-chat/Mistral — EVERYTHING incl. AGENTS memory in the mutable leading system message, task is the only user message; mined from ~/repos/mistral-vibe, the model's native harness). apply_ambient/apply_brofile_lens deleted; migration audit covers all build_exec_args/build_resume_args callers incl. bro_broadcast both branches. Adversarial review: brodex/gpt-5.5/high, 3 rounds to clean (session 6f2e4ddc). Remaining: implementation + live probes (mistral repro, after-tool cadence, responses smoke).
resolution_note: Implemented design/bro-harness/dispatch-prompt-slots.md (branch feat/dispatch-prompt-slots, commit "feat(dispatch): typed dispatch-context payload + harness-owned per-transport composition"). The daemon no longer glues directives/persona/memory onto the prompt: it passes a typed --dispatch-context payload and the harness composes per transport. On openai-chat (the failing lane) persona/standing directives/AGENTS memory/scope/pins fold into the leading system message and the operator task is the ONLY user message; per-turn directives ride the volatile tail with the existing Mistral after-tool fold. Validated: 42/42 wire-shape assertions across anthropic/openai-chat/openai-responses x first-turn/resume/bare-restore/post-compaction (capture-server harness runs); live gap repro on vibebh/mistral-medium via isolated dev daemon — one-line tasks acted on immediately, incl. multi-tool after-tool sequences; reference canons (codex rollouts, vibe session artifacts, opencode proxied wire) re-verified live and match the implemented shapes. The compounding deferred-tool friction (bbox_thread_list cold-start) is out of scope here and unchanged.
